title: Thermal Load, Capacity, and Headroom
summary: Thermal Load, Capacity, and Headroom using synthetic, simulation-only cooling infrastructure scenarios.
objectives: Interpret synthetic thermal, airflow, capacity, and dependency evidence.
Document assumptions, uncertainty, safe escalation, and validation without industrial service authority.

vocab.def: Unused modeled cooling capacity before a stated scenario limit.
Components that may share an underlying modeled failure.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This is a safe classroom simulation. Do not handle refrigerants, open liquid loops, service pumps or chillers, operate industrial controls, or intervene with facility equipment.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Use the provided synthetic thermal architecture, telemetry, capacity, redundancy, maintenance, workload, and cross-domain signals. Identify observations, dependencies, uncertainty, and modeled recovery criteria.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Document the evidence, assumptions, prohibited actions, qualified escalation, validation, and recovery criteria.

practice.prompt: What should you do when a modeled cooling condition could require industrial service?
practice.answer: Preserve the synthetic evidence and escalate to a qualified authorized role.

quiz.question: What is the safe scope of this lesson?

reflectionPrompt: What was observed, what was uncertain, and what required qualified escalation?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not HVAC or mechanical qualification.
